summary: Upright PLA cup that hangs a Surface 65 W power brick (model 1706, caliper 90.4 x 50.6 x 25.6) on the blue keyhole-slotted rack upright. The brick stands on its end, 90.4 tall, so it takes only 58 mm of rack width; its AC input faces up (top open) and its DC cable and USB-A port face down through a full-width bottom opening. It rests on 5 mm ledges under its front and back edges and is held by a 70 mm back wall and 30 mm front and side walls (a J seen from the side). Two point-down teardrop pins (9.6 mm head, 1.7 mm wide groove 5.6 mm across that grips the 1.6 mm steel), 38 mm apart in a solid column at the left end of the back wall, go into the big round holes of two keyholes and slide down. Back, front and side walls are a large diamond mesh for cooling. A small pin test sample (the pin column alone) ships with it, to check the fit before printing the holder.

assumptions: A1: keyhole sizes from the photo (D24-D26). The rev 1 sample proved the 5.6 groove, 1.7 width and 38 pitch. The 9.6 head needs the round hole to be at least ~9.8: re-print the sample to check before the holder.
A2: steel 1.6 mm (user caliper); the 1.7 mm groove leaves 0.1 mm, so the pin sits snug against the steel. If it will not slide down, the groove can open in 0.05 mm steps.
A3: the DC cable and USB-A port are on the bottom end face, within its middle 17 mm front to back (the product photo shows them there); the 5 mm ledges stay clear of them.
A4: the brick is lowered in from the top and lifted out; the AC cord plugs into its top end, which stands 20.4 mm above the back wall.
A5: pins at the left end as drawn (the cup sticks out 33 mm to the right of the pin line). It can be centred or mirrored by request.
A6: PLA softens at about 55 C; a Surface brick runs at about 40-50 C. The mesh keeps air moving: do not cover it.
A7: printer is the 180 x 180 x 180 machine used for the earlier projects, 0.4 nozzle, 0.2 layer.
